brief: Memory stocks have swung from the hottest AI trade to an unwind over several sessions. Goldman's memory basket ran from around 600 to a June peak of 2,675, then reversed to about 1,900, nearly 30% off the highs. Samsung and SK Hynix fell roughly 22% and 26% over five sessions. Foreign investors sold $11.6 billion of Korean tech over eight sessions, SK Hynix enduring 15 straight days of selling and Samsung five, while domestic institutions and retail began absorbing some of that supply. Hedge funds have been net sellers of global AI stocks for five sessions, cutting net allocation to 26.1% from a June peak of 31.7%, and the aggregate long/short ratio fell from 4.34 to 3.27, the seventh percentile over the year. Yet DDR5 spot prices keep rising even as equities fall, and Samsung and SK Hynix trade at 1.2x and 0.9x book value, suggesting the market is already pricing a downturn by 2028. China's CXMT, about 10% of global DRAM revenue, is fueling supply-shock fears, though its HBM yields and qualification remain uncertain. With the SOX oversold (RSI 34) and bullish positioning flushed out, it argues conditions for a countertrend squeeze are emerging, without guaranteeing a bottom.
